subject: Integration snag: request for trial extension & credits
messages:
From: Josh Rivera <josh@heliumpay.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine@heliumpay.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Integration snag: request for trial extension & credits

Hey Sean / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the platform looks promising and we’re excited to validate a short transaction flow in our sandbox. We started wiring the connector today but hit a blocker: our edge proxy enforces mutual TLS with SNI routing and the current Redwood SDK path doesn’t preserve the original SNI during the handshake (we're on Kong 3.1 + custom cert rotation). That means our sandbox traffic is failing TLS at the proxy layer and devs can’t complete the acceptance tests.

We’re on a tight timeline: legal wants a functional demo by the end of September to finalize procurement. Between our infra team and your docs we estimate 2–3 weeks of engineering work to patch and validate. With the trial window expiring in 10 days, that leaves us unable to properly evaluate.

Could Redwood provide: 1) a 45-day trial extension and 2) a one-time sandbox credit top-up (approx. 12k credits) so we don’t lose testing capacity while we resolve the TLS/SNI behavior? I attached a small log bundle (integration-logs-20260906.zip) showing the handshake failure and the proxy trace.

Appreciate any flexibility — this is a high-priority use case for our payments pipeline.

Thanks,
Josh Rivera
Senior Platform Engineer, HeliumPay
josh@heliumpay.com

Attachment: integration-logs-20260906.zip

Josh — appreciate the detail and the logs. Sorry you ran into this on day one. We’ll triage immediately.

Quick plan: I’ve looped in Ben (infrastructure integration) and Marissa (solutions) to assess the SNI/TLS behavior and see whether a temporary config workaround or SDK patch is faster. I’ll also start the internal approvals process for a trial extension + credit top-up — can you confirm the current trial expiry date and the approximate token burn rate for your sandbox traffic so I can include that in the request?

We aim to get you a formal answer on extension/credits within 48 hours. In the meantime, if there's any test endpoint you can share (non-prod only) we can try to repro faster.

—Sean

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration snag: request for trial extension & credits

Quick technical read from the logs Josh attached: the TLS handshake from the customer ends with an "unknown_name" alert; the proxy route expects an SNI value that matches an internal mapping we do at the load balancer layer. Our hosted connector stack currently terminates TLS in a way that normalizes SNI when we do certificate rotation, which can drop custom SNI from upstream in some proxy edge setups (rare, but hits Kong-style proxying).

Options and estimated effort:
- Short path (2–4 business days): add a lightweight passthrough flag on the ingress (config change) for affected tenants so SNI is forwarded untouched. Low risk, no code change in the runtime.
- Longer path (1–2 sprints): SDK patch to re-expose original SNI header for all outgoing connections and add tests. More robust but takes longer.

Given their timeline, the config change + a sandbox credit top-up seems the pragmatic approach. I recommend approving a 30–45 day extension and 10–15k credits so they can finish acceptance tests while we roll the passthrough flag. I can schedule the ingress change tonight if we greenlight it.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Ask: approve a 45-day trial extension and a one-time 12,000-credit sandbox top-up. This is a high-velocity opportunity; legal is already looped and this is likely to convert if the demo completes. If approved I’ll reply to Josh and schedule the ingress passthrough change with Ben tonight.

- Risk: minimal; ingress config flag reversible

Sean
